title: Sequentially Acquiring Concept Knowledge to Guide Continual Learning
abstract: arXiv:2611.33399v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The goal of continual learning (CL) is to adapt to new data (plasticity) while retaining the knowledge acquired from old data (stability). Existing methods are explicitly designed to focus on balancing stability and plasticity to mitigate the challenge of catastrophic forgetting while promoting learning. However, the impact of order and nature of samples from the new data that the network is trained on remains an under explored factor. We argue that a CL algorithm should have the ability to rank incoming samples in terms of their relationship with prior data and their effect on the learning process. In this work, we investigate if scoring and prioritizing incoming data based on their semantic relationships with the model's current knowledge can benefit CL. translated_title: 顺序获取概念知识以指导持续学习
translated_abstract: 持续学习（CL）的目标是在适应新数据（可塑性）的同时保留从旧数据中获取的知识（稳定性）。现有方法明确设计用于平衡稳定性和可塑性，以减轻灾难性遗忘的挑战，同时促进学习。然而，网络训练所使用的新数据样本的顺序和性质所带来的影响仍然是一个未被充分探索的因素。我们认为，持续学习算法应该有能力根据传入样本与先前数据的关系及其对学习过程的影响来对这些样本进行排序。在这项工作中，我们研究了根据传入数据与模型当前知识的语义关系对其进行评分和排序是否能够有益于持续学习。我们提出了SACK（Sequentially Acquiring Concept Knowledge，顺序获取概念知识），这是一种用于持续学习方法的即插即用技术。SACK将模型的类别知识分解为细粒度的……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出SACK——一种即插即用的持续学习技术，通过根据新样本与模型当前知识的语义关系对其进行评分和排序，从而指导持续学习过程。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes SACK, a plug-and-play technique for continual learning that scores and prioritizes incoming samples based on their semantic relationships with the model's current knowledge to guide the continual learning process.
